definitions.gloss: to outsmart; to outwit; to get ahead of someone by trickery
definitions.explanation: To gain an advantage over someone by acting cleverly or sneakily before they can react. Implies cunning or underhanded tactics rather than honest competition.

examples.japanese: ⟦ライバル→ライバル：11197_raibaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{出|だ}し{抜|ぬ}く。

examples.english: He always tries to get the better of people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{競合他社|きょうごうたしゃ}→競合他社：25602_kyougoutasha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{出|だ}し{抜|ぬ}かれて、⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}られて→取る：00565_toru⟧しまった。
examples.english: We were outmaneuvered by a competitor and lost the contract.

notes:
A godan verb compound of ⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to put out) and ⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧ (to pull out, to surpass). Carries a negative connotation of using cunning or underhandedness to get ahead of others. Often used in business and competitive contexts.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive — takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ to mark the person being outsmarted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦ライバル→ライバル：11197_raibaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{出|だ}し{抜|ぬ}く — to outsmart a rival
- ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{出|だ}し{抜|ぬ}く — to get the better of someone
- {出|だ}し{抜|ぬ}かれる — to be outsmarted (passive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{裏|うら}をかく→裏をかく：18296_urawokaku⟧ — to outwit, to catch off guard
- ⟦{先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ→先手を打つ：18391_sentewoutsu⟧ — to make the first move (more neutral)
- ⟦{騙|だま}す→騙す：02286_damasu⟧ — to deceive, to trick (more directly dishonest)
